# IEC 60601-2-24 — Medical Electrical Equipment — Part 2-24: Particular Requirements for Infusion Pumps and Controllers

_Demo sample data — not for clinical use._

**Standard**: IEC 60601-2-24:2012 (Edition 2.0, 2012-10-19) — see the registry distillation at [`.claude/skills/medtech-docs/references/standards/iec-60601-2-24.md`](../../../.claude/skills/medtech-docs/references/standards/iec-60601-2-24.md) for the clause map, numbering convention, and publicly verified subclause pairings
**Category**: Medical electrical equipment — particular standard to IEC 60601-1 for infusion pumps and controllers
**Recognized by FDA**: **No** — the FDA Recognized Consensus Standards database has no entry for IEC 60601-2-24 (or the AAMI ID26 variant); checked 2026-07-15 (see registry distillation Sources). Consequence for PP3500: conformance cannot be claimed via a Declaration of Conformity to a recognized standard in the 510(k); test methods drawn from this standard should be presented as performance data, with FDA's *Infusion Pumps — Total Product Life Cycle* guidance (Dec 2, 2014) as the FDA-facing content anchor. That guidance does **not** cite IEC 60601-2-24 or its subclauses.
**Module Applicability**: PP3500 pump hardware (motor drive, fluid delivery assembly, pressure sensing), pump firmware safety functions (occlusion detection, alarm annunciation, delivery accuracy control), and the dedicated administration set (anti-free-flow characteristics affect essential performance)

## Overview — Why This Standard Applies to PP3500

The PainEase PCA Advanced (PP3500) is a patient-controlled analgesia infusion pump — squarely within the standard's scope (volumetric infusion pumps; administration sets insofar as their characteristics influence basic safety or essential performance). IEC 60601-2-24 is the single most-cited verification anchor in the PP3500 risk file: the hazard analysis and design inputs invoke it for flow/bolus accuracy, free-flow protection, and occlusion alarm response.

It is listed among the applicable standards in the PP3500 Design Input Requirements header and cited by name in DI-001, DI-002, DI-006, DI-007, and DI-010.

## Open Verification Item — Subclause Numbers (blocking for Hazard Analysis Rev 1.0)

**[VERIFY]** All three specific subclause citations — **§201.12.1.101** (DI-001 / HAZ-001), **§201.12.1.103** (DI-006 / HAZ-004), and **§201.12.4.4.103** (DI-007 / HAZ-006) — require confirmation against a licensed copy of IEC 60601-2-24:2012 before Rev 1.0 of the hazard analysis is signed. This was flagged as findings E5/E6/E7 (`registry-gap`) in the hazard-analysis references audit (`docs/_analysis/pca-device/gl-tmp-rm-003-hazard-analysis-references-audit/gl-tmp-rm-003-hazard-analysis-references-audit.md`).

Publicly available evidence (publisher-authorized preview — see registry distillation) now sharpens the risk on two of the three:

1. **§201.12.1.103 as "free-flow" is contradicted**: Table 201.101 of the 2012 edition pairs 201.12.1.103 with ambulatory-pump accuracy tests. The DI-006 citation almost certainly needs to move to the correct protective-systems subclause (201.12.4.4.10x family).
2. **§201.12.4.4.103 as "occlusion alarm" is doubtful**: Table 201.101 assigns unintended-bolus + occlusion protection to 201.12.4.4.104.
3. **§201.12.1.101 is unconfirmed**: the accuracy-test family is publicly enumerated as 201.12.1.102–.107; for a volumetric (PCA) pump the applicable accuracy-test subclause is expected to be **201.12.1.102** — the .101 number may not designate the flow-accuracy test at all.

Do **not** silently renumber the citations from the public preview alone — the preview does not show the clause bodies. Resolution requires a licensed copy; until then every one of these subclause numbers carries a [VERIFY] in the documents that cite it.

A second, separate implication of the FDA-recognition check: the PP3500 submission cannot list IEC 60601-2-24 as an FDA-recognized consensus standard. Verification protocols may still use its test methods, but the 510(k) framing should follow the FDA Infusion Pumps TPLC guidance (which asks for flow-accuracy specifications, time-to-occlusion-alarm data, and free-flow/bolus hazard coverage without invoking this standard).
